As of my last update, Harry Halliday was an English cricketer born on January 22, 1855, in Shipley, Yorkshire, England. He was primarily known as a right-handed batsman.

Harry Halliday played first-class cricket for Yorkshire County Cricket Club. His first-class career, though brief, spanned from 1882 to 1883. During his tenure in first-class cricket, he participated in a total of 4 matches. In these matches, his batting performance included a total of 51 runs with a batting average of 8.50. His highest score in these few matches was 21.

While there is not a wealth of detailed information available about Halliday's broader life or cricket career beyond these basic statistics, his participation in the Yorkshire team places him among the historical roster of cricketers who have played at the first-class level.

Halliday passed away on April 20, 1943, in Scarborough, Yorkshire, England. His life spanned a period of significant changes in English cricket, though his individual contributions remain recorded primarily in the form of match records and statistics.
